definitions.explanation: Severe difficulty, distress, or suffering, especially over a prolonged period. A literary and formal word emphasizing endurance through difficult circumstances.

examples.japanese: {困苦|こんく}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{耐|た}える→耐える：12087_taeru⟧。
{困苦|こんく}⟦{欠乏|けつぼう}→欠乏：15114_ketsubou⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{生活|せいかつ}→生活：01443_seikatsu⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{送|おく}った→送る：00742_okuru⟧。
examples.english: They lived a life of hardship and privation.

examples.japanese: ⟦{幼少期|ようしょうき}→幼少期：21168_youshouki⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{困苦|こんく}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{乗|の}り{越|こ}えて→乗り越える：04620_norikoeru⟧、⟦{彼|かれ}→彼：01292_kare⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{立派|りっぱ}→立派：01093_rippa⟧な⟦{人物|じんぶつ}→人物：03356_jinbutsu⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{成長|せいちょう}→成長：03290_seichou⟧⟦した→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: Overcoming the hardships of his childhood, he grew into a fine person.

notes:
A literary compound of ⟦{困|こま}る→困る：00861_komaru⟧ (to be troubled) and {苦|く} (suffering). Used in formal writing and speeches, not in everyday conversation. Often appears in historical and biographical narratives describing difficult living conditions.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {困苦|こんく}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{耐|た}える→耐える：12087_taeru⟧ — to endure hardship
- {困苦|こんく}⟦{欠乏|けつぼう}→欠乏：15114_ketsubou⟧ — hardship and want
- {困苦|こんく}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{乗|の}り{越|こ}える→乗り越える：04620_norikoeru⟧ — to overcome hardship
- {困苦|こんく}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{生活|せいかつ}→生活：01443_seikatsu⟧ — a life of hardship

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{苦労|くろう}→苦労：02672_kurou⟧ — hardship, trouble; the most common everyday word for difficulty and hard work
- ⟦{苦難|くなん}→苦難：25318_kunan⟧ — suffering, ordeal; similar formality level, focuses on painful trials
- {辛苦|しんく} — toil, hard labor; emphasizes the painful effort involved
- {難儀|なんぎ} — difficulty, trouble; can also mean troublesome or arduous
